reasoning: All six failure-driven edits are kept unchanged. Their anchors exist in the current skill and do not overlap. Four of the five success-driven edits are kept because they cover patterns the failure edits do not: letter-count hints, unseen-media clues and bare proper-noun clues in Rule 1; the passage-title shortcut, headword and fill-in-the-blank definitions, and truncated archive clues in Rule 3. The success edit giving people's full first and last name is dropped. The failure edit on first name plus surname, with popular nickname forms, already covers it. I changed one phrase in the headword bullet from 'in the singular' to 'singular unless the clue's noun is plural' so it agrees with the failure-driven grammatical-number rule. No edit touches the protected SLOW_UPDATE section.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content:
- SLOT CHECK (do this before writing the answer): read the grammar of the clue to decide what KIND of thing is missing, then answer with that kind.
  - 'He / She / His / Her / Who ...' with no other noun -> a PERSON (the performer, author or leader behind the songs, works or events in the clue). A work or song title quoted in the clue is an anchor, never the answer ('He recorded "I Walk The Line"' -> the singer, Johnny Cash).
  - 'this nation / country / state / city / sport / fruit / phenomenon' -> exactly that category. 'A causeway connects this Persian Gulf nation to ...' -> the nation (Bahrain), not the causeway's name, even if passages mention the causeway most often.
  - If the whole answer string would be just a word or phrase already written in the clue, you probably picked the wrong slot. If the clue contains a foreign-language word (e.g. 'Ananas', 'L'Ananas') and asks for 'this fruit / food / thing', answer with the English name for it (Pineapples), not the foreign word.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content:
- Strip the thing that is merely attached to the answer. 'The university of this U.S. territory is home to X' -> the territory ('Guam'), not 'University of Guam'. 'This man sued ... over his daughter's school' -> the man's name ('Oliver Brown'), not the school or the issue. 'This state's flag / this city's team / this author's novel' -> the state, city or author.
- 'This way / this kind / this many / this often' asks only for the adverb, adjective or number ('backwards'), not the phrase it modifies ('country music backwards'). Test: substitute your answer for 'this way' in the clue; it should read naturally without repeating clue words.
- 'This person/thing, like X' or 'a letter to this person, like X': X is only an example. The answer is the role or category noun that X belongs to ('the editor' for Ben Bradlee), not X itself. Read the passages for X's job or title.

edits.target: ## Rule 3: Look for the clue repeated verbatim in the context
edits.content:
- Archive/flashcard text is often run together with no separator: '<clue text> Rainbow This "platinum-dome" character ...' or '<CLUE IN CAPS>, SOUTH SEA...'. The answer is the short span immediately after the end of the clue, before the next clue or sentence begins. Take that span exactly ('Rainbow', not 'Rainbow Serpent' pulled from a neighbouring Wikipedia passage).
- If the verbatim archive answer is cut off by '...' or by the snippet limit, complete it to the full standard name using other passages, and use the clue's own quoted word as a hint ('SOUTH SEA...' + clue 'this "bubble"' -> 'South Sea Bubble'). Do not submit the truncated fragment.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content:
- FORM CHECKS (apply last):
  - Answer with the bare category word that the clue noun names. Do not attach a league, brand, language or myth-name qualifier: 'this sport' -> 'Football' (not 'NFL football'); 'this phenomenon seen in the sky' -> 'Rainbow' (not the myth's longer name 'Rainbow Serpent').
  - EXCEPTION to 'only the missing part': when the clue puts the head noun of a proper name in quotation marks ('this "bubble"', 'this "war"'), the answer is the full standard name including that word ('South Sea Bubble'). A leading 'the' is fine if it is part of the usual name.

edits.target: - Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones'.
edits.content:
- Match the grammatical number of the clue's noun. Use the singular for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'). Use the plural when the clue says 'these', 'species of these', 'ones', 'group of ...', 'muscles', 'set of ...', when the slot is a type of thing that comes in groups (mascots, animals, fruits or crops used as ingredients), and for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas', 'Bears', 'Pineapples'). 'This group of muscles at the back of the thigh' -> 'the hamstrings'.
- Specificity: when the context repeatedly gives a more specific official or standard name for the referent (a species, a state symbol, a named variant), use that full name, e.g. 'Brown pelican' rather than just 'pelican'. This overrides 'shortest form' when the qualifier is part of the standard name in the passages. Still drop pure descriptor words such as 'song', 'film' or 'band', and league/brand qualifiers.

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - For people, give first name plus surname. If the passages or headlines use a well-known nickname form of the first name (Jimmy, Bill, Babe), use that popular form ('Jimmy Doolittle') rather than the formal first name. Do not give a surname alone unless the context's verbatim answer is just the surname.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content:
- A trailing number in parentheses, e.g. 'He spun straw into gold(15)', is a LETTER COUNT hint for the answer (or sometimes a clue number). It is not part of the question. Use it only to check that a candidate fits (count letters, ignoring spaces). 'Rumpelstiltskin' has 15 letters, which confirms it.
- If the clue refers to media you cannot see ('the structure seen here', 'shown here', 'this picture/map/audio'), ignore that part. Answer from the remaining textual descriptors (e.g. 'used as a bleach', 'simple links') plus the entity the passages tie to them. Combine this with your own knowledge when it agrees with the context, and never reply that the image is missing.
- A clue that is just one bare proper noun (e.g. 'Timonium', a town, landmark or region) is a category-style clue. Answer with the larger entity that all the passages tie it to: a town or landmark -> its state or country, a region -> its country. Never reply that the clue is incomplete.

edits.target: A phrase repeated across independent passages is strong evidence.
edits.content: - Use passage titles ([TLE]) as a shortcut. When several passages are titled after, or centred on, one entity and also repeat the clue's specifics (dates, numbers, quoted titles), that entity is the answer. Give its plain name ('Erewhon', 'Padre Island', 'Charles Evans Hughes') without extra descriptors.

edits.target: Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Definition-style clues ('This unit is equal to...', 'It's the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line', '3 points on one throw in horseshoes', 'the crime for which X is condemned') want the single term the description defines. Look for a dictionary or glossary snippet whose wording nearly matches the clue, or for the term the passages repeatedly pair with the key descriptors. Answer with that entry's HEADWORD (the title such as 'Man-hours - definition of...', or the bolded term before the colon), singular unless the clue's noun is plural, and in the passage's spelling ('man-hour', 'Homestretch', 'ringer', 'trapezoid'). Do not answer with a word from inside the definition ('hour', 'minute'), a description, or a longer phrase. If the clue has a blank ('House Committee on ___ & Infrastructure'), answer with only the blank's word ('Transportation').

edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - If the archived clue is cut off ('...') before its answer, match the clue's remaining concrete details (numbers, units, years, quoted titles) against the other passages. Take the concept they all tie to those details; for example, '51.5 kilometers' appears with 'Olympic distance' passages -> 'Triathlon'. Answer with that concept, not with a nearby number or an unrelated page.
